title: NULL Handling & Three-Valued Logic
description: Master SQL's Three-Valued Logic (TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN), handle missing data with COALESCE, NULLIF, and safe equality operators.

data.text: In SQL, `NULL` does not mean zero, an empty string, or false. `NULL` represents an **unknown or missing value**. Because of this, SQL operates on **Three-Valued Logic (3VL)**, where boolean expressions can evaluate to `TRUE`, `FALSE`, or `UNKNOWN`.
The NULL Comparison Trap: Why `x = NULL` is Never True

Comparing any value to `NULL` using the equality operator (`=`) yields `UNKNOWN`. Even `NULL = NULL` evaluates to `UNKNOWN`! Because the `WHERE` clause only keeps rows that evaluate to `TRUE`, writing `WHERE col = NULL` will always return zero rows.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Never use `=` or `!=` with `NULL`; always use `IS NULL` or `IS NOT NULL`.
Use `COALESCE` to provide default fallbacks for nullable columns.
Use `NULLIF(denominator, 0)` to eliminate division by zero exceptions.
